invariant: A bracket inside a sequence arrow is one ordered arrow-configuration expression, not a color literal. CommandArrow captures the complete bracket body independently of the arrow shaft and applies it after deriving the shaft's base body, heads, direction, and decorations. CommandArrow.applyStyle tokenizes the body on commas. At the pinned Java revision, `dashed` and `dotted` select ArrowBody.DOTTED, `hidden` selects ArrowBody.HIDDEN, `bold` is accepted without changing the configuration, and every other accepted token is resolved as a color; later tokens operate on the configuration produced by earlier tokens. Color and body are therefore orthogonal and survive together for ordinary, self, reversed, bidirectional, and external sequence messages. The bracket is part of the arrow header only, so Creole anchors such as `[[#anchor label]]` in message text are not arrow styles.
causal_divergence: The original Rust parser treated an inline bracket as a color-only annotation, so `-[#C2185B,dashed]>` became invalid color `#C2185B,dashed` plus a solid body; external parsing discarded the bracket. Commit 59169b2a introduced typed source-order tokens, but its correction scans the entire pre-colon header and removes the first style-looking bracket anywhere. Java's CommandArrow grammar captures ARROW_STYLE only between ARROW_BODYA and ARROW_BODYB, after PART1 and before PART2. The fresh quoted-participant counterexample therefore leaves `Source [hidden]: 9401` intact in Java but Rust strips `[hidden]` from the participant and loses the first message. Three additional orthogonality gaps surfaced. First, SeqParser::autoactivation_for handles only Solid and Dotted; Java CommandArrow tests the head and then treats every non-dotted body, including HIDDEN, as activation under `autoactivate on`. Second, the fresh right-to-left bidirectional message is parsed as BOTH but Rust paints only one head when the source lies geometrically right of the target; ComponentRoseArrow draws both dressings for BOTH_DIRECTION independent of spatial order. Third, Rust's first-participant offset for a found message uses only the label width, while Java Step1MessageExo builds its arrow component from AbstractMessage.getLabelNumbered, so the bold autonumber prefix and gap also reserve left extent. These causes explain the rejected review's quoted-name failure, missing receiver activation/nesting and 39.3628px found-message offset, and one-element bidirectional deficit. The bold self-message itself is byte-equivalent on reinspection; the preceding bidirectional group caused the shifted structural diff.
